insight.title: The Relativity Trap
insight.subtitle: How your brain negotiates with reality.

sections.text: Why does a ten-minute wait feel like an eternity at a coffee shop, but vanish when you’re scrolling on your phone? Your brain ignores absolute time, focusing instead on the hidden system of relativity.

This is the Contrast Effect. Your nervous system is wired to detect changes rather than constants. You don’t experience the world as it is; you experience the deviation from your most recent mental baseline.

This pattern dictates your daily satisfaction. A "good" day is often just a day that was slightly better than yesterday. When you understand this, you realize your frustration is rarely about the event itself.

Try this today: When you feel a surge of impatience or disappointment, pause for one second. Ask yourself, "What am I comparing this to?" Simply acknowledging the comparison instantly weakens the emotional grip.
The weight of a problem is rarely determined by its size, but by the scale you use to measure it.
